title: Orthogonal decomposition by coordinates
statement: Let $\Omega$ be a finite set with probability mass function $\pi$, let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, and let $f\colon\Omega^n\to\mathbb{R}$. A family of functions $f_S\colon\Omega^n\to\mathbb{R}$ indexed by subsets $S$ of the $n$ coordinates is an orthogonal decomposition of $f$ if their sum is $f$, each $f_S$ depends only on the coordinates in $S$, and, whenever $T$ is a proper subset of $S$, the product-space inner product of $f_S$ with every function depending only on coordinates in $T$ is zero.
hypotheses_covered: A family of functions indexed by subsets of the $n$ coordinates
caveat: The supplied snippet omits the definitions of coordinate dependence and the product-space inner product, so their precise conventions cannot be confirmed.
